newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Olympics-IOC starts Sydney inspection tour.
newsitem.headline: Olympics-IOC starts Sydney inspection tour.

text.p: International Olympic Committee inspectors began a three-day mission on Monday to assess Sydney's progress in preparing for the 2000 Olympic Games.

It was the first IOC inspection visit since the ill-starred Atlanta Games, which were marred by the kind of traffic, transport and technical problems that Sydney Games organisers are anxious to avoid.
Earlier this month, a regional politician was appointed to head the Sydney organising committee after the resignation of committee president and businessman John Iliffe.

The appointment of Michael Knight, the New South Wales Olympics minister, was said to have the full backing of IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch -- who is keen that the Sydney Games has the government support lacked by Atlanta.
An 11-strong delegation, headed by Coordination Commission chairman and leading IOC member Jacques Rogge, toured several Olympic sites on its first day in Sydney.
The group inspected the proposed base for the yachting regatta on Sydney Harbour and a 43,000-capacity stadium which has been earmarked to host one of the qualifying groups for the soccer tournament.
They also looked at sections of the proposed courses for the marathon and cycling road race.
"Commission members were shown sites which they had not seen on the two previous fact-finding visits to Sydney," a spokesman for the Sydney organising committee told Reuters.

The Commission has twice visited over the past 12 months and will monitor progress with further visits every six months until 2000. To ensure closer coordination with IOC headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland, the IOC also plans to send small working parties even more frequently.
Rogge will give a news conference on Wednesday after a briefing with Sydney Olympic officials on Tuesday.
The New South Wales state government, as underwriters of the Games, has budgeted to spend A$1.9 billion (US$1.5 billion) on infrastructure to stage the Olympics in Sydney.
Construction of the 110,000-seat main Olympic stadium at Homebush in Sydney's western suburbs began two weeks ago. The stadium, costing A$665 million, is expected to be ready by June 1999.
